title.en: Australia news live: Labor MPs gather before Victorian leadership challenge; PM praises outgoing ACTU ‘giants’
title.zh: 澳大利亚新闻直播：工党议员在维多利亚州领导权挑战前集结；总理赞扬即将离任的ACTU‘巨头’

summary.en: Victoria's Premier, Jacinta Allan, faces a leadership challenge from her deputy, Ben Carroll, amidst ongoing political developments. Separately, the Prime Minister has commended outgoing 'giants' from the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), as its president, Michele O’Neil, prepares to depart.
summary.zh: 维多利亚州州长雅辛塔·艾伦正面临副手本·卡罗尔的领导权挑战，政治局势持续发展。与此同时，总理赞扬了即将离任的澳大利亚工会理事会（ACTU）的‘巨头’们，其中包括其主席米歇尔·奥尼尔。

body.en: The Victorian premier, Jacinta Allan, will be challenged by her deputy, Ben Carroll. Follow updates live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast ACTU president says now is the ‘right time’ to leave Michele O’Neil, the president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions, said it’s the “right time” to leave after she announced her departure alongside ACTU secretary Sally McManus . We thought about this and we just think that it’s time for renewal. The union movement is in good shape. We’ve seen changes in workers’ rights that have made a big difference in workers’ lives. We’ve seen the union movement starting to grow for the first time in decades. And next year will be the 100th anniversary of the ACTU. So we think it’s time for a new leadership team to come in. We have a debt heading towards $200bn in this state. We have teachers out striking in the streets because the state government and Ben Carroll can’t secure a pay deal. We have holes in the roads. You need a majority government to fix those problems, and you need someone with a plan. Now he might performatively call a royal commission tokenistically, now that he’s become leader, but that’s not out of sincere concern about corruption. That’s out of sincere concern about the polls and what that means for Victorian Labor. Continue reading...
body.zh: 维多利亚州州长杰辛塔·艾伦 (Jacinta Allan) 将受到副手本·卡罗尔 (Ben Carroll) 的挑战。关注实时更新 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 ACTU 主席表示，现在是离开的“正确时机” 澳大利亚工会理事会主席米歇尔·奥尼尔 (Michele O’Neil) 在与 ACTU 秘书 Sally McManus 一起宣布离职后表示，现在是离开的“正确时机”。我们思考了这个问题，认为是时候进行更新了。工会运动状况良好。我们已经看到工人权利的变化给工人的生活带来了巨大的变化。我们看到工会运动几十年来首次开始发展。明年将是 ACTU 成立 100 周年。因此，我们认为是时候组建新的领导团队了。我们州的债务接近 2000 亿美元。我们有教师走上街头罢工，因为州政府和本·卡罗尔无法达成薪酬协议。我们的道路上有洞。你需要多数政府来解决这些问题，并且需要有计划的人。现在，既然他已经成为领导人，他可能会象征性地召开皇家委员会，但这并不是出于对腐败的真诚担忧。这是出于对民意调查及其对维多利亚工党意味着什么的真诚担忧。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As political and organizational leadership shifts, we are reminded that positions of influence are ultimately held by divine appointment. Yahweh is the one who raises up and brings down leaders, guiding the course of nations and institutions. In times of transition, we can trust in His sovereign hand over all authority.
reflection.zh: 当政治和组织领导层发生变动时，我们被提醒，有影响力之职位最终由雅伟所设立。雅伟是那位兴起和降下领袖的，祂指引着国家和机构的进程。在过渡时期，我们可以信靠祂对所有权柄的至高掌管。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: DNC chair faces growing scrutiny amid financial pressure and internal turmoil
title.zh: 民主党全国委员会主席因财政压力和内部动荡面临日益严格的审查

summary.en: Ken Martin, the chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), is facing increased scrutiny due to financial difficulties and internal disagreements regarding the party's future direction.
summary.zh: 民主党全国委员会（DNC）主席肯·马丁正面临日益严格的审查，原因是该党面临现金流问题以及对未来方向的内部意见分歧。

body.en: Fraught time for Ken Martin as new reporting details cash-flow problem and divisions over party’s direction Mounting financial pressures and growing internal turmoil at the Democratic National Committee (DNC) have intensified scrutiny of chair Ken Martin, as new reporting detailed a deepening cash-flow problem, management concerns and widening divisions over the party’s direction less than 100 days before the November midterm elections. The latest reporting has underscored both the committee’s financial distress and the toll it has taken on Martin personally. The New York Times reported that the embattled DNC chair, who took the helm last year, became the subject of an internal HR inquiry after throwing his phone in the direction of a junior aide’s desk during a heated exchange in early July, prompting a formal complaint. The Times, citing people familiar with the matter, also reported that the incident nearly cost him his job and has contributed to growing isolation with the party as the committee grapples with mounting financial strain. Continue reading...
body.zh: 新报告详述了现金流问题和党派方向分歧，肯·马丁 (Ken Martin) 面临着严峻的考验 民主党全国委员会 (DNC) 日益严峻的财务压力和日益严重的内部动荡，加剧了对主席肯·马丁 (Ken Martin) 的审查，距离 11 月中期选举不到 100 天，新报告详细介绍了日益严重的现金流问题、管理层的担忧以及党派方向分歧不断扩大的情况。最新的报告凸显了该委员会的财务困境以及它给马丁个人带来的损失。 《纽约时报》报道称，这位去年接任的民主党全国委员会主席在七月初的一次激烈交锋中将手机扔向一名初级助手的办公桌方向，引发了正式投诉，之后成为了内部人力资源调查的对象。 《泰晤士报》援引知情人士的话报道称，这一事件几乎让他丢掉了饭碗，并且在该委员会应对日益严重的财务压力之际，他与该党的关系日益疏远。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times of financial strain and internal disagreement, effective leadership requires more than just authority; it demands a multitude of wise counselors. As this political committee faces scrutiny and division, the need for sound guidance and unity in direction becomes critical. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us that collective counsel can provide stability and...
reflection.zh: 在财政紧张和内部意见分歧的时期，有效的领导力需要的不仅仅是权力，更需要众多智者的建议。当这个政治委员会面临审查和分裂时，对正确指导和方向统一的需求变得至关重要。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，集体的谋划可以为组织提供稳定，防止其衰落。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: France and Spain race to contain huge wildfires before fresh heatwave begins
title.zh: 法国和西班牙争分夺秒，赶在新一轮热浪前控制大规模野火

summary.en: Firefighters in France and Spain are urgently working to control massive wildfires. Officials state that the coming days are “absolutely critical” as they race against time before a new heatwave is expected to intensify the blazes and complicate their efforts.
summary.zh: 法国和西班牙的消防员正紧急扑灭大规模野火。官员表示，未来几天“至关重要”，因为他们必须赶在新一轮热浪来临之前控制火势，以免火情进一步恶化，增加扑救难度。

body.en: Coming days are ‘absolutely critical’ for firefighters before temperatures rise again this week, officials say Firefighters in France and Spain are racing to bring huge wildfires under control before another heatwave this week that will complicate efforts to tame the flames. Spain’s interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, said Monday and Tuesday were “absolutely crucial days” before temperatures rise again from Wednesday. Continue reading...
body.zh: 官员们表示，在本周气温再次上升之前，未来几天对消防队员来说“绝对至关重要”，法国和西班牙的消防队员正在加紧努力，在本周另一场热浪到来之前控制住巨大的野火，这将使扑灭大火的工作变得更加复杂。西班牙内政部长费尔南多·格兰德·马拉斯卡表示，周一和周二是“绝对关键的日子”，周三气温将再次上升。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As firefighters battle relentless blazes and brace for another heatwave, their endurance is tested to the limit. In such moments of overwhelming challenge, we are reminded that Yahweh offers renewed strength to those who hope in Him, enabling them to run and not grow weary. May those on the front lines find this divine resilience as they work to protect...
reflection.zh: 当消防员们奋力扑灭无情大火并准备迎接新一轮热浪时，他们的耐力正受到极限考验。在这样巨大的挑战面前，我们被提醒，雅伟赐予那些仰望祂的人新的力量，使他们奔跑却不困倦。愿这些在前线的人们在保护生命和土地时，能找到这份来自雅伟的韧性。

verse.textEn: Those who hope in Yahweh will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary.
verse.textZh: 但那等候雅伟的，必从新得力。他们必如鹰展翅上腾。

title.en: Trump warns of return to ‘strong military action’ if Iran diplomacy fails
title.zh: 特朗普警告若伊朗外交失败将恢复“强硬军事行动”

summary.en: Washington and Tehran have issued conflicting messages regarding the status of talks aimed at resolving the Middle East crisis. Donald Trump has reiterated his warning that the US will resort to "strong military action" against Iran if diplomatic efforts do not swiftly resolve the situation.
summary.zh: 华盛顿和德黑兰就结束中东危机的谈判状况发布了相互矛盾的信息。唐纳德·特朗普再次警告称，如果外交努力不能迅速解决危机，美国将对伊朗恢复“强硬军事行动”。

body.en: Washington and Tehran issue conflicting messages over the status of talks to end Middle East crisis Donald Trump has once again warned that the US will return to “strong military action” against Iran if diplomatic efforts do not bring a rapid resolution to the crisis in the Middle East. “We are in very deep talks with Iran. If they don’t work out, we will go back to very strong military action,” the US president told Axios on Monday. Asked for how long he would allow the talks to proceed, he answered: “Not much time. Either it goes fast or not at all.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 华盛顿和德黑兰就结束中东危机的谈判状况发出相互矛盾的信息唐纳德·特朗普再次警告称，如果外交努力不能迅速解决中东危机，美国将重新对伊朗采取“强有力的军事行动”。 “我们正在与伊朗进行非常深入的谈判。如果谈判不成功，我们将重新采取非常强有力的军事行动，”美国总统周一告诉 Axios。当被问及他允许谈判进行多长时间时，他回答说：“时间不多。要么进展快，要么根本不进行。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news reminds us of the constant human effort required to maintain peace amidst international tensions. The pursuit of diplomatic solutions, even when difficult, reflects the biblical call to "live peaceably with all, if possible, so far as it depends on you." It underscores the importance of seeking peaceful resolutions as our primary endeavor,...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻提醒我们，在国际紧张局势中维持和平需要持续的人类努力。寻求外交解决方案，即使困难重重，也反映了圣经中“若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦”的呼召。它强调了将寻求和平解决方案作为我们首要任务的重要性，同时承认其中涉及的复杂性。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: A Japanese town wrestles with identity after protests over its first mosque
title.zh: 一座日本小镇在首次清真寺引发抗议后，正在与身份认同作斗争

summary.en: As Japan increasingly relies on foreign workers, it is also grappling with how to integrate new cultures and religions. A town's identity is being questioned following protests over the construction of its first mosque.
summary.zh: 随着日本越来越依赖外国劳工，它也在努力应对如何融入新的文化和宗教。一座小镇在首次清真寺引发抗议后，正在与自身身份认同问题作斗争。

body.en:
Today, it's a field of grass. But soon, it'll be the site of the first mosque in this Japanese town.

"It makes me worry about how our community might change," says long-time resident Noriko Izumizawa.

Plans to build an Islamic religious site in Fujisawa, a laid-back seaside town about an hour's drive south of Tokyo, have sparked a wide range of emotions.

There is anger and fear, as well as hope and acceptance, exposing the growing anxieties over immigration and social change as Japan grapples with a labour shortage from a shrinking and ageing population.

Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive, Japan is increasingly relying on foreign workers to fill open jobs. That means an influx of immigrants with various cultures, languages, religions and ways of being.

So the debate that is playing out in towns like Fujisawa across the country is one that goes to the heart of how Japan sees itself.

Izumizawa is not alone in the way she feels. She is among a group of Fujisawa residents who are anxious about the increasingly visible Muslim community. She says that the polarising debates around immigration in the US and Europe have also contributed to her unease.

Earlier this year, anti-mosque protests flared up at the local train station, where thousands took to the streets to object to the proposed construction of the mosque. Some argue that a mosque much larger than the nearby Japanese Shinto shrine is disrespectful.

There have also been reports of hate speech and misinformation spreading on Japanese social media. Local outlets say mosques have been receiving abusive phone calls and emails, some of which has prompted anti-hate groups to organise counter protests calling for no hate.

Hiroki Suzuka, who manages a coffee shop opposite the road where the Fujisawa mosque is set to be built, calls for greater understanding and dialogue.

"I'm not particularly opposed, but I wouldn't say I'm strongly in favour either," Suzuka said.

"I think the first step is to learn about them, what Islam is, what kind of people they are, and what values and perspectives they hold. It begins with having an open mind and a desire to understand each other."

Businessman Mohamed Mohideen has lived in Osaka for the past 39 years. He moved from his home country Sri Lanka in 1987 for better work opportunities during the economic bubble.

He has dealt gemstones and later worked in trade, exporting used cars to countries like Sri Lanka and Pakistan.

But Mohideen feels that compared to back then, local people have become hostile and started making hurtful remarks at Muslims, both online and in person.

"On social media, there are countless comments like, 'Get out of Japan' and 'Go back to your own country,'" Mohideen said. "People have also started coming...
body.zh: 今天，这里是一片草地。但很快，这里将成为这个日本小镇第一座清真寺的所在地。 “这让我担心我们的社区可能会发生什么变化，”长期居民泉泽纪子说。 在东京以南约一小时车程的休闲海滨小镇藤泽建立伊斯兰宗教场所的计划引发了广泛的情绪。 在日本努力应对人口萎缩和老龄化造成的劳动力短缺之际，愤怒和恐惧、希望和接受，暴露了人们对移民和社会变革日益增长的焦虑。 尽管移民仍然具有政治敏感性和限制性，但日本越来越依赖外国工人来填补空缺职位。这意味着具有不同文化、语言、宗教和生活方式的移民涌入。 因此，在全国各地像藤泽这样的城镇上演的争论是一场触及日本如何看待自己的核心问题的争论。 泉泽并不孤单有这种感觉。她是藤泽居民中的一员，他们对日益明显的穆斯林社区感到焦虑。她说，美国和欧洲围绕移民问题的两极分化辩论也加剧了她的不安。 今年早些时候，当地火车站爆发了反清真寺抗议活动，数千人走上街头反对修建清真寺的提议。一些人认为，一座比附近的日本神社大得多的清真寺是不尊重的。 还有报道称，仇恨言论和错误信息在日本社交媒体上传播。当地媒体称，清真寺不断收到辱骂电话和电子邮件，其中一些促使反仇恨团体组织反抗议活动，呼吁不要仇恨。 铃鹿弘树 (Hiroki Suzuka) 在即将修建藤泽清真寺的道路对面经营一家咖啡店，他呼吁加强理解和对话。 “我并不是特别反对，但我也不会说我强烈支持，”铃鹿说。 “我认为第一步是了解他们，了解伊斯兰教是什么，他们是什么样的人，以及他们持有什么价值观和观点。首先要有开放的心态和相互理解的愿望。” 商人穆罕默德·莫希丁 (Mohamed Mohiden) 已在大阪生活了 39 年。 1987 年，他在经济泡沫时期从祖国斯里兰卡移居，寻求更好的工作机会。 他从事过宝石交易，后来从事贸易工作，向斯里兰卡和巴基斯坦等国家出口二手车。 但莫希丁认为，与那时相比，当地人已经变得充满敌意，并开始在网上和当面发表对穆斯林的伤害性言论。 “社交媒体上有无数的评论，比如‘滚出日本’和‘回到你自己的国家’，”莫希丁说。 “人们也开始来了......

reflection.en: As communities navigate the integration of new cultures and religions, the challenge often lies in how to welcome those who are different while preserving local identity. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to treat foreigners residing among us as native-born, loving them as ourselves. This principle calls for a spirit of hospitality and understanding,...
reflection.zh: 当社区在融合新文化和宗教时，挑战往往在于如何在保留地方身份的同时欢迎异己。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，要将居住在我们中间的外国人视同本地人，爱他们如同爱自己。这一原则呼唤着好客和理解的精神，在不断演变的社会中培养和平与相互尊重。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Number of suspects in fatal Seattle food festival shooting rises to three
title.zh: 西雅图美食节致命枪击案嫌疑人增至三人

summary.en: Authorities have identified three suspects in connection with a fatal shooting at a Seattle food festival. One suspect is in custody, another is being sought, and a third is believed to have died at the scene, according to court documents.
summary.zh: 法庭文件显示，西雅图美食节致命枪击案的嫌疑人数量已增至三人。其中一名嫌疑人已被拘留，第二名正在被追捕，第三名据信已在现场死亡。

body.en:
Seattle police say they now believe at least three people were involved in a fatal shooting at a food festival on Sunday.

Police initially said two suspects were thought to have been shooting at each other at the annual Bite of Seattle food festival at the Space Needle - one of the city's most popular tourist spots.

However, court papers relating to the arrest of one of these, a 15-year-old, on Monday revealed they now think there is a third. One is still being sought by police, while the other is thought to have been killed at the scene.

Three people were killed in the shooting and at least four others were injured, including a two-year old boy.

The teenage suspect made an initial appearance in court on Monday and has been remanded in custody pending trial.

During the hearing, police revealed in court documents that they believe that three suspects may have fired shots during the "gunfight".

Court papers filed by the police say investigators are searching for "at least one other unknown suspect," according to local media.

The three people who died on Sunday were a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man, and a 56-year-old woman, according to the authorities. Two deaths were confirmed at the scene, and one person died later in hospital.

Sunday was the final day of the annual three-day free food festival, which draws some 350,000 people each year.

Videos shared online showed people crouched on the ground, taking cover behind pillars and shelves of merchandise in the Space Needle's lobby during the shooting.

Several witnesses told a local TV station affiliated to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, that they heard multiple shots before running away.

"At first, thought there were fireworks, and then everybody flooded and ran past us," Nick Bate told the TV station.

Leanne Coles another witness told the station she used the Space Needle to try to keep track of where she was.

"Everybody started running, and so we just ran too, and we ran through the garden and we ducked and we decided to keep running with the crowd," she said.

Faith Adia Hunter told Associated Press that one of the shooters was near her and her friends when they heard the shots, sending them fleeing for shelter in the Seattle Children's Museum.

"We were right next to him when it started so we took off running," she said. "So, we took off running too into the building with the crowd."

The Seattle Police Department said an investigation remains ongoing and urged the public to avoid the area.

Mayor Katie Wilson said in a statement that she wanted to "thank the Seattle police officers who responded to the scene and took a suspect into custody".

title.en: US singer D4vd to go on trial for murder in death of teen
title.zh: 美国歌手D4vd将因谋杀青少年而受审

summary.en: A US singer is facing a murder trial after being accused of killing Celeste Rivas Hernandez, whose remains were discovered in a Tesla registered to his address.
summary.zh: 一名美国歌手将因涉嫌谋杀一名青少年而受审，受害者塞莱斯特·里瓦斯·埃尔南德斯的遗骸在其名下的一辆特斯拉汽车中被发现。

body.en:
A judge has ruled that US musician D4vd will go on trial for murder over the death of a teenage girl.

The decision came after a five-day preliminary hearing, in which Los Angeles prosecutors questioned a dozen witnesses and displayed photographic evidence as 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez's family watched on.

The star, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, is accused of killing the girl, whose remains were found last September in a Tesla registered to his address.

Burke, 21, has pleaded not guilty to charges of murdering and sexually abusing her.

Burke's arraignment is scheduled for 31 August. The trial is to start within 90 days of that date.

Prosecutors have alleged Burke stabbed the teen before dismembering her body after years of alleged sexual abuse.

They allege he killed her because the teen had threatened to reveal his relationship with a minor and destroy his multi-million dollar music career.

Evidence read in court on Monday showed threats Celeste made to Burke on 22 April 2025, stemming from arguments about his friendship with another girl.

"I swear to GOD I will kill u", one expletive-laden text said, followed by a threat to strangle him and tell her dad lies about him. "i will end ur career and ur life I will damage anything", one text said.

The following day, Hernandez went to Burke's Hollywood home in an Uber he had sent to pick her up.
body.zh: 法官裁定美国音乐家 D4vd 因谋杀一名少女而受审。 这一决定是在为期五天的初步听证会后做出的，在听证会上，洛杉矶检察官询问了十几名证人，并在 14 岁的塞莱斯特·里瓦斯·埃尔南德斯 (Celeste Rivas Hernandez) 的家人旁观下展示了照片证据。 这位明星的法定姓名是大卫·安东尼·伯克，他被指控杀害了这名女孩，去年 9 月在登记在他地址的一辆特斯拉汽车中发现了女孩的遗体。 21 岁的伯克对谋杀和性虐待她的指控表示不认罪。 伯克定于 8 月 31 日受审。审判将于该日期后 90 天内开始。 检察官指控，伯克在多年遭受性虐待后，先刺伤了这名少女，然后肢解了她的尸体。 他们声称他杀了她，因为这名青少年威胁要揭露他与一名未成年人的关系，并毁掉他价值数百万美元的音乐事业。 周一在法庭上宣读的证据显示，塞莱斯特于 2025 年 4 月 22 日对伯克发出威胁，原因是他与另一名女孩的友谊发生争执。 一条充满咒骂的短信写道：“我向上帝发誓，我会杀了你。”随后威胁要勒死他，并告诉她父亲关于他的谎言。一条短信写道：“我会结束你的职业生涯和你的生活，我会破坏任何东西。” 第二天，埃尔南德斯乘坐伯克派来接她的优步前往伯克在好莱坞的家。

title.en: Trump says Iran war talks taking place during lull in strikes
title.zh: 特朗普称伊朗战争谈判是在罢工间歇期进行的

summary.en: The US president says "there is a good chance that something could happen", as Iran denies direct talks are taking place.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said "there are very friendly negotiations going on" about the conflict with Iran, after the warring sides did not exchange strikes for a third straight day.

He expressed optimism for an end to the war on Monday, telling reporters aboard Air Force One: "I think there's a good chance that something could happen."

However, he warned that Washington would "go back to doing what we were doing" before the pause in fighting if the latest negotiations failed.

Trump said he had decided to pause US strikes on Iran on Friday because the countries mediating between them had asked him to give the talks another chance.

The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.

The US military said at the time that its strikes were aimed to "degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz" - a global route for transporting oil.

The price of oil on Monday fell by more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point on hopes the conflict could be de-escalated.

Aboard the presidential plane, Trump also dismissed media reports that after five months of fighting, US ammunition stockpiles were now running low.

"We have a lot of ammunition. We have a lot of the mid-level stuff too, more than we could ever use, no matter what," Trump said. "But we have a lot. I'd like to have more."

He said a "lot of equipment" was being built, in particular Patriots - highly valued US-made anti-ballistic missiles.

Meanwhile, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said the US military "has more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of President Trump's strategic goals and beyond, and Operation Epic Fury has exposed what happens when you mess with the United States."

"Even still, the president has urged our defence contractors to constantly produce more made-in-America weapons, which are the best in the world," the spokesperson added.

The US and Israel launched their strikes against Iran on 28 February. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles and drones on US military bases and other assets located in Gulf states, as well as on targets inside Israel.

In June, Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding to stop military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.

But after Iranian forces attacked tankers in the waterway on 13 July, Washington resumed air strikes against Iran and reinstated its naval blockade of the country's ports.

Tehran retaliated with attacks on US military facilities and bases across the Middle East, killing four American soldiers. The US strikes have since killed dozens of people, according to Iran's health ministry.
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，在交战双方连续第三天没有相互攻击后，关于与伊朗的冲突“正在进行非常友好的谈判”。 周一，他对结束战争表示乐观，并在空军一号上告诉记者：“我认为很有可能会发生一些事情。” 不过，他警告说，如果最新的谈判失败，华盛顿将在暂停战斗之前“回到我们正在做的事情”。 特朗普表示，他决定周五暂停美国对伊朗的打击，因为在两国之间进行调解的国家要求他再给会谈一次机会。 此次停火是在美国近两周的每日罢工和针锋相对的攻击之后进行的，这实际上破坏了 6 月份达成的停火协议。 美国军方当时表示，其袭击目的是“削弱伊朗威胁霍尔木兹海峡商业航运的能力”——霍尔木兹海峡是全球石油运输路线。 由于人们希望冲突能够缓和，周一油价一度下跌 9% 以上，至每桶 87.59 美元。 在总统专机上，特朗普还驳斥了媒体报道，称经过五个月的战斗，美国弹药库存现已所剩无几。 “我们有很多弹药。我们也有很多中级装备，无论如何，都超出了我们的使用范围，”特朗普说。 “但我们有很多。我想要更多。” 他说，正在建造“大量设备”，特别是爱国者导弹——价值很高的美制反弹道导弹。 与此同时，白宫发言人安娜·凯利表示，美国军方“拥有足够的弹药、弹药和库存来服务于特朗普总统的所有战略目标及其他目标，而史诗般的愤怒行动已经暴露了当你惹恼美国时会发生什么。” 发言人补充说：“即便如此，总统仍敦促我们的国防承包商不断生产更多美国制造的武器，这些武器是世界上最好的。” 2月28日，美国和以色列对伊朗发动袭击。德黑兰进行报复，向位于海湾国家的美国军事基地和其他资产以及以色列境内的目标发射导弹和无人机。 6月，伊朗和美国签署了一份谅解备忘录，停止军事行动并重新开放霍尔木兹海峡，并达成协议在接下来的60天内结束战争。 但在7月13日伊朗军队袭击水道中的油轮后，华盛顿恢复了对伊朗的空袭，并恢复了对该国港口的海上封锁。 德黑兰对美国在中东的军事设施和基地发动袭击进行报复，造成四名美国士兵死亡。据伊朗卫生部称，美国的空袭已造成数十人死亡。

title.en: As the US pauses the war with Iran, is Trump really running out of weapons?
title.zh: 随着美国暂停与伊朗的战争，特朗普的武器真的用完了吗？

summary.en: The US has fired thousands of hard-to-replace missiles during its war with Iran. We unpack whether its "arsenal of freedom" is perilously low.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
When US President Donald Trump took the stage earlier this month at the Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit, flanked by the CEOs of some of America's largest defence firms, he had one message in mind: build more weapons, and build them faster.

"We have the best quality in the world," Trump told the armsmakers gathered at the US Army War College, with 'Secretary of War' Pete Hegseth at his side. "But we need a little more speed."

The Trump administration framed the summit as part of a two-pronged approach to revitalise American industry and bolster US warfighting capabilities and, in Hegseth's words, its "arsenal of freedom".

Largely unspoken, however, was the vast expenditure of sophisticated and difficult-to-manufacture weapons used during nearly 40 days of intense combat operations in Iran during Operation Epic Fury earlier this year and tit-for-tat strikes that have taken place since. So far, the US government says the war has cost $37.5bn (£28bn), and the vast majority of that has been spent on munitions.

By the time a tenuous ceasefire took effect on 8 April, US forces had struck over 13,000 targets across Iran, according to the White House. American air defences intercepted over 1,700 Iranian drones and ballistic missiles over the same period.

Now, the US has paused its strikes on Iran to allow negotiations to go ahead. A New York Times report says that Trump was advised to shelve plans to escalate the conflict as it would further drain American stockpiles.

On Monday, Trump denied there was a shortfall, telling the Wall Street Journal: "We have far more munitions than anyone in the world, and far more than we need."

This has been a touchy subject for some time within the US administration. Last month, when pressed on the subject, Hegseth denied that supplies were thinning out.

His position seems to have changed since. Last week, he told the Senate Appropriations Committee that the Pentagon needed another $87bn (£68bn) to address "critical shortfalls", including equipment.

Exact ammunition expenditures and remaining stockpiles remain classified. But publicly available data compiled by the Washington DC-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) paints a stark picture of depleted stockpiles that, in the short-term, are difficult to replace.

"It depends on the munition - but one to five years [to make a single missile] is the bottom line," says Mark Cancian, a retired Marine Corps colonel and senior adviser at CSIS who has been researching the issue. "And there's nothing you can do to speed that up."

But is the US really eating through ammunition so fast that it may struggle to fulfil its military duties and objectives?

title.en: Trump tries optimism as foes hold fire and Iran denies peace talks
title.zh: 敌人开火、伊朗否认和谈，特朗普试图保持乐观

summary.en: Fighting between the US and Iran has been paused since the weekend. While Trump expressed hope for a deal, Iran has remained unmoved.

body.en:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday voiced optimism at the prospects for a negotiated peace deal with Iran, as the two sides held their fire for a third consecutive day.

Fighting between the longtime foes has been paused since Saturday after 13 nights of renewed US strikes on the Islamic republic sparked by a breakdown in diplomacy over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

But the US leader expressed hope that renewed diplomacy could bring an end to the war that began in late February with a wave of US-Israeli strikes, rattling both the region and the global economy.

"I have a lot of patience... We'll see what happens," he said aboard Air Force One.

Iran had earlier denied that there were any direct talks with the US to end the conflict.

"Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us regarding current developments in the region. But at present, we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States," said Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.

Trump told the US news outlet Axios that mediating countries had asked him to hold fire to give diplomacy a chance, adding: "We are in very deep talks with Iran."

Aboard Air Force One he said that if the new efforts failed, "we go back to doing what we were doing" before the pause in fighting.

On that subject, he dismissed concerns that US ammunition stockpiles were running low nearly five months after war broke out.

"We have a lot of ammunition. We have a lot of the mid-level stuff too, more than we could ever use no matter what," he said.

Despite the recent lull, Saudi Arabia came under attack on Monday, with its defence ministry saying it had intercepted several drones fired by Iran-linked groups in Iraq targeting oil facilities.

No group claimed responsibility, but the Saudis called on Baghdad to prevent such attacks from being launched from its territory.

Pakistan, which has been mediating a resolution to the Middle East war, condemned the drone attacks, saying they "pose a grave threat to peace and stability" in the Middle East.

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels also said they launched drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom's drones. Saudi Arabia is yet to comment on the claim.

Saudi Arabia and other Gulf nations accused pro-Iran militias in Iraq of launching waves of attacks on their territory during the conflict's earlier phase, but the groups haven't claimed any attacks in the region since the resumption of hostilities.

title.en: As wildfires ravage Europe, here's the latest advice for travellers
title.zh: 欧洲野火肆虐，旅行者最新建议

summary.en: Wildfires are causing significant disruption across Europe during its peak holiday season, prompting Australian travelers to seek updated information and review their travel insurance policies.
summary.zh: 欧洲多地野火肆虐，正值旅游旺季，澳大利亚游客被敦促及时了解情况并检查旅行保险。

body.en:
As hundreds of thousands of people flee fast-moving wildfires across Europe, Australians heading overseas are being urged to stay informed, monitor official travel advice and understand what their travel insurance covers if their plans change.

More than 330,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain as fires burn through popular holiday destinations, closing roads, delaying flights and forcing communities to flee. Authorities have also issued fresh evacuation orders near the historic Spanish city of Toledo, while firefighters continue battling major blazes around Bordeaux in southwestern France.

The fires have intensified during Europe's busy summer holiday period, with airports, major roads and tourist destinations among those affected as emergency services race to contain the blazes.

In France, more than 220,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires continue to burn through the Gironde region, home to vineyards, coastal towns and the popular tourist destination of Cap Ferret.

French interior minister Laurent Nuñez described the situation as "very unfavourable", warning the fire was moving towards Bordeaux, although authorities have so far ruled out evacuating the city itself.

The blaze came within about 15km of Bordeaux's outskirts over the weekend, prompting police to go door-to-door in nearby communities to evacuate residents.

Travel has also been disrupted, with Bordeaux Airport reporting widespread delays after air traffic restrictions were introduced to allow firefighting aircraft to operate safely.

Spain is also grappling with multiple major blazes, with more than 115,000 people evacuated and another 30,000 ordered to shelter in place.

The largest fire, in the central province of Ávila, has burned more than 50,000 hectares, making it the country's biggest wildfire in recent history. Fires continue to burn near Madrid and in the eastern province of Castellón.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has announced a civil protection emergency will be declared in the affected central regions, unlocking additional recovery funding.

More than 150,000 hectares have burned across Spain since the start of the year — six times the area destroyed over the same period last year.

Australian travellers are being urged not to panic, but to closely monitor conditions, remain flexible and understand what their travel insurance does — and doesn't — cover if their plans are disrupted.

title.en: Chad's government says it's withdrawing from the ICC

summary.en: Chad's Foreign Ministry has announced plans to leave the International Criminal Court. It said that its effectiveness was "limited and uneven." Chad's leader is a military officer accused of repressing the opposition.

title.en: Indian youth score a win over Modi with humor and grit
title.zh: 印度年轻人用幽默和勇气战胜了莫迪

summary.en: Driven by social media satire, the Gen-Z-led "Cockroach" protest movement spurned by grievances over an exam scandal caused a shake-up in India's government. DW spoke with a few protesters in New Delhi.

body.en:
Driven by social media satire, the Gen-Z-led "Cockroach" protest movement spurned by grievances over an exam scandal caused a shake-up in India's government. DW spoke with a few protesters in New Delhi.

Walking from Jantar Mantar to Connaught Place in central New Delhi on Saturday evening provided an unusual sight for the prime corridor of power in the world's largest democracy.

Satirical posters mocking India's legislative, executive and judiciary were plastered on the walls, and the pavement was sprayed with sometimes "vulgar" graffiti mocking Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

These were all remnants of thousands of young Cockroach movement protesters who had flooded the streets hours earlier after India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned .

Celebrating Pradhan's resignation, which had been a core protest demand , some protesters were heard telling security officials "see you at the next protest," coming only days after several people were injured in clashes with baton-wielding police who fired tear gas into crowds.

Instagram was also full of images from cities across India with young people dancing in front of police officials to the line "Everybody knows that I'm a good girl, officer " from Lana Del Ray's song "Playing Dangerous."

Others held posters reading: "Cuff me, daddy" and some were seen climbing atop police barricades.

The movement, known as the Cockroach Janta Party movement (CJP) , came after the chief justice of India referred to unemployed young people as "cockroaches" in an offhand remark. The name is also a play on Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Since a scandal broke in May involving a highly competitive university entrance exam, the Gen Z protests have spread across India, challenging the political establishment with Instagram reels, viral trends, sarcastic jingles and posters.

"In our generation humor has become the defense mechanism from pain, frustration and helplessness. This entire protest is driven by humor, driven by Instagram and social media," Karan Azad, a 24-year-old law student, told DW at the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.

Another protester held a sign addressed to Modi reading in transliterated Hindi: "Buddy, you can't even make tea," alluding to Modi's boyhood days as a tea seller.

"I had to do my part. I am the youth. If we don't stand up for ourselves no one else will, we have to fight this battle ourselves," the female protester with the sign told DW without giving her name.

A protester named Tushar, also 24, said he wasn't "afraid of a backlash" from the authorities, but rather "would have had FOMO [fear of missing out]" had he not joined the protest.

title.en: Ghana's community service bill: A fix for the prison crisis?
title.zh: 加纳的社区服务法案：解决监狱危机？

summary.en: The community service bill offers community service as an alternative to prison sentences, particularly for minor offenses. It's meant to decongest Ghana's prisons and prevent overcrowding once it's signed into law.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The community service bill offers community service as an alternative to prison sentences, particularly for minor offenses. It's meant to decongest Ghana's prisons and prevent overcrowding once it's signed into law.

Ghana's parliament recently passed the Community Service Bill , 2026. The piece of legislation is designed to introduce community service as an alternative to custodial sentences for minor offenses. The bill also seeks to ease pressure on the country's overcrowded prisons and reshape how justice is administered for minor crimes .

The legislation establishes a National Community Service Secretariat and provides a legal framework for courts to impose community service in Ghana instead of imprisonment for specified offenses.

According to the government, the move will reduce the financial strain of maintaining prison facilities, which have long suffered from inadequate budgets, high medical costs and chronic congestion .

"If you check the current prison population, overcrowding is over 37%. We have a current population of over 13,000 prisoners. Today the cost of maintaining them, feeding them alone, requires 10 million cedis (€752,000, $859,000)  a quarter," Ghana's Interior Minister, Muntaka Mubarak, who tabled the bill in parliament , told the house during a debate.

Under the bill, community service applies to offenses punishable by not more than three years' imprisonment, with or without a fine. Courts may also impose community service for offenses that carry fines alone or fines combined with imprisonment.

This means petty crimes such as false publication or traffic offenses could now attract noncustodial penalties.

Legal practitioner Christian Malm Hesse described the bill as "a step in the right direction," noting its potential to reduce prison overcrowding .

He told DW that the bill provides a structured alternative for misdemeanor offenses that previously defaulted to custodial sentences.

However, some Ghanaians believe that its effectiveness will depend on proper categorization of offenses and public education.

According to DW correspondent Eric Mawuena Egbeta, many Ghanaians still need clarity on which offenses qualify.

"An offense which is higher than a misdemeanor would mean that you will not get a community sentence… A lot more persons would need education on it," Egbeta said.

For legal practitioners like Hesse, one key safeguard in the bill is the requirement for a social inquiry report, which helps judges assess an offender's background, circumstances and suitability for community service. body.zh: 社区服务法案提供社区服务作为监禁刑罚的替代方案，特别是对于轻微犯罪。一旦签署成为法律，其目的是缓解加纳监狱的拥挤状况并防止过度拥挤。 加纳议会最近通过了《2026 年社区服务法案》。该法案旨在引入社区服务，作为轻罪监禁刑罚的替代方案。该法案还旨在缓解该国过度拥挤的监狱的压力，并重塑对轻微犯罪的司法管理方式。 该立法设立了国家社区服务秘书处，并为法院在加纳实行社区服务而不是对特定罪行进行监禁提供了法律框架。 政府表示，此举将减轻维护监狱设施的财政压力，监狱设施长期以来一直遭受预算不足、医疗费用高昂和长期拥堵的困扰。 加纳内政部长蒙塔卡·穆巴拉克在议会辩论中向议会提交了该法案，他表示：“如果你检查一下目前的监狱人口，就会发现监狱过度拥挤的程度超过 37%。我们目前有超过 13,000 名囚犯。如今，维持这些囚犯的费用，仅是喂养他们，就需要四分之一的 1,000 万塞地（752,000 欧元，859,000 美元）。” 根据该法案，社区服务适用于可判处三年以下监禁、并处或不处罚款的犯罪行为。法院还可以对单独罚款或罚款与监禁相结合的犯罪行为实行社区服务。 这意味着虚假发布或交通违法等轻微犯罪现在可能会受到非监禁处罚。 法律从业者克里斯蒂安·马尔姆·黑塞 (Christian Malm Hesse) 将该法案描述为“朝着正确方向迈出的一步”，并指出其有可能减少监狱过度拥挤。 他告诉德国之声，该法案为以前默认判处监禁的轻罪提供了一个结构化的替代方案。 然而，一些加纳人认为，其有效性将取决于对犯罪行为的适当分类和公共教育。 德国之声记者 Eric Mawuena Egbeta 表示，许多加纳人仍然需要明确哪些罪行符合资格。 埃格贝塔说：“比轻罪更严重的罪行意味着你不会被判社区刑……更多的人需要这方面的教育。” 对于像黑塞这样的法律从业者来说，该法案的一项关键保障是要求提供社会调查报告，这有助于法官评估罪犯的背景、情况和社区服务的适合性。黑塞表示，此类措施可确保量刑决定的知情性和一致性，从而降低任意判决的风险……

title.en: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
title.zh: 藤森在中美平衡之际掌管秘鲁

summary.en: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. As she takes office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. As she takes office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.

When Keiko Fujimori steps into the presidential office on Tuesday, she'll bring back a political movement that hasn't been in power for more than a quarter century.

Fujimorism, a mix of neoliberalism, populism and strict government policies, characterized the 1990-2000 presidency of her father, the late Alberto Fujimori. Keiko Fujimori is stepping in amid a climate of social polarization, with promises to deliver more security, economic recovery and improvements in the health and education sectors.

But beyond those domestic projects, Fujimori is taking charge at a time of increased strategic importance for Peru . The country has become one of the key battlegrounds in the growing competition between the United States and China for political influence in South America.

Fujimori has already signaled that security will be the top priority for her government.

On the agenda: more video surveillance, a stronger police presence, tougher punishment for crimes and organized gangs, and command and control centers across the country. Part of the crackdown includes the construction of four mega-prisons, like those in El Salvador .

Eliana Carlin, a political science expert at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru in Lima, is concerned by how Fujimori's plans will affect human rights .

"Behind [these measures] lie strong ideological positions intended to justify making the police and the armed forces solely subject to military jurisdiction," she said.

In addition to a stronger focus on security, Fujimori has said she intends to advance infrastructure projects, attract private investment, build new schools and hospitals and modernize the country with the help of technology and artificial intelligence .

But delivering on these pledges depends largely on whether the government can find the necessary funds. Infrastructure and essential services continue to face significant deficits. Added to that is the surging crime rate and the threat of the strengthening El Nino weather pattern , which could hit Peru with increased drought, extreme heat , flooding and other climate-related disruptions.

Foreign policy will also be a major challenge for Fujimori's administration. The opening of the Chancay port and logistics hub has turned Peru into a strategic player in regional trade — and made it a central focus in the geopolitical rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

body.en:
Iran says it is still in control of the Strait of Hormuz and not ‌seeking to resume peace talks with the United States.

Following 13 successive nights of intensifying bombing that provoked Iran to fire ‌on US bases in response, Trump halted the campaign over the weekend.

Iran said it would pause its own attacks for as long as the US pause in bombing endures.

Trump's decision to suspend the campaign reflected advice from his top brass ‌that the bombing, aimed at breaking Iran's grip on the strait, had reached the limits of what it could achieve, according to a US official and widespread US media reports.

The US official told Reuters that military commanders had advised the president they were running out of targets.

The official said the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine, had also expressed concern over the depletion of air defence weapons used to protect US bases in the region.

Similar reports indicating that civilian and military aides had advised Trump to halt the campaign were carried over the weekend by the New York Times, CNN, Axios and other news outlets.

The US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, said on ‌Sunday Trump had paused ‌the campaign to allow room for negotiations.

But ⁠the spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, Esmail Baghaei, said in a televised press conference on Monday that Iran had not asked to resume peace talks with the United States.

The end of the US bombing campaign sent oil prices tumbling in the hope that disrupted global supplies could resume flowing.

Brent crude, which had briefly ticked above AU$150 a barrel last week for the first time since May, fell around 7.8 per cent by mid-morning on Monday to just under AU$130.

But in a clear bid to signal that the US bombing had failed in its objective, Tehran indicated it was still in control of the world's most important waterway for energy markets.

Several Iranian state media outlets carried the same report, citing an "informed source" as saying that Iran had turned around six "offending ships" on Monday morning that had attempted to cross the strait without ⁠its permission.

"As previously announced, the traffic route in the Strait ‌of Hormuz is the route specified by Iran, and other routes are contaminated and have no way out," the Iranian state media reports quoted the source as saying.

Trump launched his renewed bombing campaign to punish Iran after Tehran fired on ships using a route through the strait that ‌has been promoted by the United States, which has told vessels to sail close to the coast of Oman.

title.en: Israeli settlers torch two mosques in West Bank during a deadly surge in violence
title.zh: 以色列定居者在致命暴力激增期间焚烧约旦河西岸两座清真寺

summary.en: Violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has escalated since the Gaza war began, with recent incidents including Israeli settlers setting fire to two mosques.
summary.zh: 自加沙战争爆发以来，以色列占领的约旦河西岸暴力事件激增，近期事件包括以色列定居者焚烧了两座清真寺。

body.en:
Two mosques in the Israeli-occupied West Bank were set on fire overnight in an apparent Israeli settler attack, officials said overnight, after a spate of deadly violence that killed four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers.

Palestinians and the Israeli opposition accuse Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hard-line government of turning a blind eye to attacks by settlers against Palestinians , which threaten to ignite widespread violence across the territory.

Israeli soldiers and police fanned out across the West Bank after the attack, closing off major roads and blocking access to a hospital. Israel also arrested more than 70 Palestinians over the weekend.

The mosques, in the villages of Qusra and Kour in the northern West Bank, suffered extensive damage in the fires.

In Qusra, the attackers spray-painted "revenge Benayahu," referring to one of the settlers killed on Friday, and "the land of Israel is redeemed with blood".

Ahmed Abu Mahmoud, 64, who lives next to the Qusra mosque, said he heard noises at 3am and discovered the mosque had been set on fire. The fire was too large for him to fight on his own, so he called for help.

"The military arrived here, saw with their own eyes and then left," Mahmoud said.

He added that the attackers spray-painted Hebrew graffiti on the mosque's walls, including the word "revenge".

Security footage in Kour obtained by The Associated Press showed three people dressed in civilian clothes setting off a large explosion in the entrance of the mosque in the middle of the night.

In a separate incident, Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque in the village of Kour, near Tulkarem, and spray-painted racist slogans on its walls, according to the Palestinian ministry of religious affairs.

The ministry said that "groups of settlers burned a mosque in the village of Kour in Tulkarem governorate and wrote racist slogans on its walls".

Israel's military said it was working with police to investigate the mosque attack.

"The security forces strongly condemn incidents of this kind, including harm to religious sites, and will continue to act decisively to maintain security and public order in the area," it said.

The Israeli army often announces investigations into violence against Palestinians but rarely makes arrests or prosecutes settlers involved in violence.

reflection.zh: 约旦河西岸悲剧性的暴力循环，以焚烧圣地等行为为标志，凸显了在不被邪恶吞噬的情况下回应邪恶的深刻挑战。雅伟呼召我们打破这种模式，寻求以良善与和平的行为来战胜仇恨和破坏。

title.en: ‘I thought it didn’t stand a cat’s chance in hell’: Andrew Ridgeley on Wham’s surreal trip to China
title.zh: ‘我以为它根本没有一丝希望’：安德鲁·里奇利谈威猛乐队超现实的中国之旅

summary.en: Four decades after Wham! became the first Western pop act to tour China, Andrew Ridgeley reflected on the surreal experience, including silent gigs and awkward embassy receptions. He also recalled the “bloody ludicrous” hiring of Lindsay Anderson as director for the 1985 trip.
summary.zh: 威猛乐队成为首个在中国巡演的西方流行乐队四十年后，安德鲁·里奇利回顾了那次超现实的经历，包括沉默的演出和尴尬的使馆招待会。他还回忆起1985年那次旅行中“荒谬至极”地聘请林赛·安德森担任导演。

body.en: Four decades after he and George Michael became the first western pop act to tour the country, Ridgeley recalls silent gigs, awkward embassy receptions – and the ‘bloody ludicrous’ hiring of Lindsay Anderson as director Wham! special – read about George Michael’s great lost superstar duets album There has always been something surreal about Wham!’s 1985 trip to China. George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley looked like alien visitors on the streets of Beijing, their bouffant hair and flamboyant outfits setting them apart from the Mao jackets and drab uniforms of the Chinese people they encountered. Now the full strangeness of the duo’s brief trip, which made them the first western pop act to play in the country, is explored in a fascinating documentary film, Wham! 10 Days in China. Using previously unseen archive footage and featuring new interviews with many of the people involved in the tour, it shows the extraordinary impact Wham!’s two concerts had on their Chinese audience, as well as providing a snapshot of a country on the brink of great change. Continue reading...
body.zh: 里奇利和乔治·迈克尔成为第一个在中国巡演的西方流行艺人四十年后，里奇利回忆起无声的演出、尴尬的大使馆招待会，以及聘请林赛·安德森担任导演的“极其荒唐”的事。威猛乐队 1985 年的中国之行总是给人一种超现实的感觉。乔治·迈克尔（George Michael）和安德鲁·里奇利（Andrew Ridgeley）在北京街头看起来就像外来的访客，他们蓬松的头发和华丽的服装使他们与他们遇到的中国人的毛泽东夹克和土褐色制服截然不同。现在，一部引人入胜的纪录片《威猛！》（Wham！中国10天。它使用了以前未公开的档案片段，并对参与巡演的许多人进行了新的采访，展示了威猛乐队的两场音乐会对中国观众的非凡影响，并提供了一个处于巨大变革边缘的国家的快照。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Wham!'s pioneering tour of China was a venture into uncharted cultural territory, marked by both novelty and unexpected challenges. When we commit our plans and endeavors to Yahweh, we acknowledge that even the most ambitious or unusual projects can find their purpose and direction. This reminds us that every step into the unknown, whether personal or...
reflection.zh: 威猛乐队对中国的开创性巡演是一次进入未知文化领域的尝试，充满了新奇和意想不到的挑战。当我们把自己的计划和努力交托给雅伟时，我们承认即使是最雄心勃勃或不寻常的项目也能找到其目的和方向。这提醒我们，无论是个人还是文化上，每一步迈向未知都可以信赖更高的智慧。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Watch: Scaffolding tumbles from Hong Kong building as Typhoon Noul makes landfall
title.zh: 观看：台风“诺尔”登陆香港，脚手架从大楼坠落

summary.en: Typhoon Noul, described by state media as the strongest to hit China this year, caused scaffolding to collapse from a building in Hong Kong as it made landfall.
summary.zh: 据官方媒体报道，台风“诺尔”是今年迄今为止登陆中国的最强台风，在香港登陆时导致一栋建筑的脚手架倒塌。

body.en:
Police said they received numerous calls after multi-storey scaffolding along Cheung Sha Wan Road collapsed in powerful winds on Saturday. No injuries have been reported.

Typhoon Noul made landfall in southern China on Sunday morning, lashing the region with strong winds and heavy rain and forcing Hong Kong airport to cancel around 360 passenger flights.

The typhoon is the strongest to make landfall in China in 2026 to date, according to state media.
body.zh: 警方表示，周六长沙湾道多层脚手架在强风中倒塌后，他们接到大量报警电话。目前还没有人员受伤的报告。 台风诺尔周日早上在中国南部登陆，给该地区带来强风和大雨，迫使香港机场取消约360个客运航班。 据官方媒体报道，这场台风是迄今为止在 2026 年登陆中国的最强台风。

reflection.en: The destructive power of a typhoon reminds us of creation's vulnerability and the forces that cause it to groan. In such moments, we are reminded of the wider suffering in the world, and our longing for restoration.
reflection.zh: 台风的破坏力提醒我们，受造界是脆弱的，并且有使其呻吟的力量。在这样的时刻，我们被提醒世上更广泛的苦难，以及我们对复兴的渴望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
title.zh: 柏林骄傲：最新一连串致命车辆袭击事件

summary.en: The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.

A Christopher Street Day event in the German capital, which attracts thousands of people every year, was attacked on Saturday night by a 21-year-old suspect who police said was associated with the "Islamist scene" in Berlin. One person was killed and another 16 people were injured, while the suspect, named as Abdul B., fled the scene.

Two people were killed and 20 more injured in early May when a car drove through a crowd in the eastern German city of Leipzig. The suspect in the case was described as a 33-year-old German national and local resident, who had been known to police, though not for relevant offenses.

At least two people were killed and several were injured in the southwestern German city of Mannheim in 2025 when a motorist intentionally drove his car into a crowd of people , according to police and public prosecutors. Authorities identified the suspect as a 40-year-old German man. Law enforcement ruled out a political motive at the time, though the man had paid a fine under Germany's hate crime laws for a comment he made on a social media platform in 2018.

A 37-year-old woman and her two-year-old daughter were killed in Munich in February last year when a car was rammed into a demonstration organized by the trade union Verdi. A 25-year-old Afghan man subsequently went on trial for their murder, as well as the attempted murder of the dozens of other people injured in the attack. 

A vehicle plowed into a crowd of New Orleans revelers early on New Year's Day 2025, killing 14 people and injuring dozens of others. The driver of the vehicle and two police officers were killed in a firefight soon after the attack, which took place at about 3:15 in the morning local time. The FBI said it was investigating the incident as an act of terrorism.

At least six people died and more than 300 were injured when a man slammed a rented BMW SUV into a Christmas market in eastern Germany. The suspect, who was arrested at the scene, was a 50-year-old doctor originally from Saudi Arabia who had expressed anti-Muslim views and support for the far-right AfD party. In June 2026, he was sentenced to life in prison, with the court noting the severity of his crime, which more or less rules out the possibility of an early release.

body.zh: 柏林骄傲活动中的袭击只是一长串将车辆用作武器的事件中的最新一起。近年来，美国、加拿大和中国也发生过类似的攻击。 德国首都的克里斯托弗街日活动每年都会吸引数千人参加，周六晚上，该活动遭到一名 21 岁嫌疑人的袭击，警方称该嫌疑人与柏林的“伊斯兰主义现场”有关。造成 1 人死亡、16 人受伤，嫌疑人 Abdul B. 逃离现场。 5 月初，德国东部城市莱比锡一辆汽车驶过人群，造成两人死亡、二十多人受伤。据描述，该案嫌疑人是一名 33 岁的德国国民和当地居民，警方认识他，但并未因相关罪行而认识他。 据警方和检察官称，2025 年，德国西南部城市曼海姆一名驾车者故意驾车冲撞人群，造成至少两人死亡、多人受伤。 当局确认嫌疑人是一名 40 岁的德国男子。执法部门当时排除了政治动机，尽管该男子因 2018 年在社交媒体平台上发表的评论而根据德国仇恨犯罪法缴纳了罚款。 去年2月，慕尼黑工会威尔第组织的一场示威活动中，一辆汽车被撞，导致一名37岁的妇女和她两岁的女儿丧生。一名 25 岁的阿富汗男子随后因谋杀以及企图谋杀袭击中受伤的其他数十人而接受审判。 2025 年元旦早些时候，一辆汽车冲撞了新奥尔良狂欢者的人群，造成 14 人死亡、数十人受伤。袭击发生在当地时间凌晨 3 点 15 分左右，车辆司机和两名警察在袭击发生后不久的交火中丧生。 联邦调查局表示，正在将此事件作为恐怖主义行为进行调查。 一名男子将一辆租来的宝马 SUV 撞向德国东部的圣诞市场，造成至少 6 人死亡、300 多人受伤。现场被捕的嫌疑人是一名来自沙特阿拉伯的 50 岁医生，曾表达反穆斯林观点并支持极右翼选择党。 2026 年 6 月，他被判处终身监禁，法院注意到他罪行的严重性，这或多或少排除了提前释放的可能性。 2024 年 11 月 11 日，一名 62 岁的司机驾驶一辆小型 SUV 撞向在中国南方一个体育场馆锻炼的人们，造成 38 人死亡，这是该国多年来最致命的大规模凶杀案。另有 48 人受伤。当局表示，肇事者情绪激动……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

title.en: From the strait of Hormuz to the North Sea, a global maritime war rages around us – and more than the price of oil is at stake | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 从霍尔木兹海峡到北海，一场全球海上战争在我们身边肆虐——不仅仅是石油价格受到威胁

summary.en: A recent report highlights the breakdown of international maritime cooperation, warning of a global maritime conflict extending from the Strait of Hormuz to the North Sea. The article notes that the US military is actively protecting merchant shipping from Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, indicating a wider...
summary.zh: 一份最新报告指出，国际海上合作正在瓦解，并警告一场全球海上冲突正从霍尔木兹海峡蔓延至北海。文章提到，美国军方正在霍尔木兹海峡积极保护商船免受伊朗袭击，这表明基于规则的秩序正在更广泛地崩溃。

body.en: The collapse of the rules-based order is not confined to the land: we’re imperilled as centuries of maritime cooperation sink beneath the waves The US military campaign to protect merchant shipping from Iranian attacks by asserting direct maritime control in the strait of Hormuz is not an idea unique to Donald Trump’s administration. Almost exactly 200 years ago, in the period 1825-27, a powerful US naval squadron led by Commodore John Rodgers was sent to the Mediterranean to defend American ships from the depredations of Greek corsairs and pirates. For all the new-minted republic’s brave talk of liberty, the US squadron did not assist Greece’s ongoing “regime change” struggle for independence from the Ottoman empire. Its sole, self-serving purpose was to defend US trade, markets and business interests. After abandoning his call for a people’s revolution in Tehran , this, too, is what Trump’s reckless war with Iran has now boiled down to. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...
body.zh: 基于规则的秩序的崩溃不仅限于陆地：随着几个世纪的海上​​合作沉入海浪之下，我们面临危险美国通过对霍尔木兹海峡实施直接海上控制来保护商船免受伊朗袭击的军事行动并不是唐纳德·特朗普政府独有的想法。几乎整整 200 年前，即 1825-27 年期间，由准将约翰·罗杰斯 (John Rodgers) 率领的一支强大的美国海军中队被派往地中海，保护美国船只免受希腊海盗和海盗的掠夺。尽管这个新成立的共和国勇敢地谈论自由，但美国中队并没有协助希腊正在进行的争取从奥斯曼帝国独立的“政权更迭”斗争。其唯一的、自私的目的是捍卫美国的贸易、市场和商业利益。在放弃了德黑兰人民革命的呼吁之后，特朗普与伊朗的鲁莽战争也归结为这一点。西蒙·蒂斯达尔是卫报外交事务评论员继续阅读...

Yet, Psalm 46:9 reminds us that Yahweh ultimately has the power to make wars cease, breaking weapons and bringing an end to conflict. This offers a profound hope that even in the face of widespread tension,...
reflection.zh: 全球海上战争和国际秩序崩溃的消息可能令人感到不知所措，似乎冲突正成为常态。然而，诗篇46:9提醒我们，雅伟最终有能力止息战争，折断弓、折断枪，使冲突终结。这在面对普遍紧张局势时，提供了一个深刻的希望，即通过神圣的干预，更大的和平是可能实现的。

A Vietnamese-registered cargo ship carrying 62 crew members sank near Yongshu Reef in the South China Sea, one of the world's most important and contested maritime spaces.

Rescuers were searching on Sunday for 17 people missing after a Vietnamese ship sank in the South China Sea , China's ⁠state media reported.

Authorities in the Chinese island province of Hainan said the cargo vessel Khoi ​Nguyen 18 ran into trouble near Yongshu Reef, also known as Fiery Cross Reef, state broadcaster CCTV said.

The ship was carrying 62 crew members, and 45 people were rescued from the water.

Vietnamese authorities arrived at the scene immediately after the cargo ship "sank while operating in bad weather conditions in the East Sea," Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Pham Thu Hang said in a statement to AFP news agency.

A Chinese rescue ship, the Nanhai Jiu 115, first spotted what was believed to be a distress flare from the vessel shortly before 6:30 pm on Saturday (1030 GMT).

The Khoi Nguyen 18 is a Vietnamese-registered ship measuring just under 70 meters (230 feet) in length, according to state news agency Xinhua.

It added that six Chinese vessels, a rescue helicopter and a Vietnamese vessel were involved in the search-and-rescue operations.

Hang said that authorities and fishing vessels were "actively searching for the remaining people."

Beijing claims sovereignty over almost the entire South China Sea, despite the 2016 international ruling, initiated by the Philippines against China, that its assertion has no legal basis.

One of the most highly contested areas is the ​ Spratly Islands , which China calls the Nansha Islands, where China has built runways ⁠and militarized artificial islands.

But ​Beijing's sweeping claims to the busy waterway overlap with those of other countries, including Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia and Taiwan .

title.en: Typhoon Noul forces more than 715,000 from homes and cancels hundreds of flights in China and Hong Kong
title.zh: 台风“诺尔”迫使逾71.5万人撤离家园，中港数百航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Noul, the strongest to hit China this year, made landfall over the weekend, bringing severe winds and heavy rain to southern China and Hong Kong. The storm forced over 715,000 people from their homes and led to hundreds of flight cancellations.
summary.zh: 今年迄今为止登陆中国的最强台风“诺尔”于周末登陆，给华南地区和香港带来了强风暴雨。这场风暴导致超过71.5万人被迫撤离家园，数百趟航班被取消。

body.en:
Typhoon Noul made landfall early Sunday bringing strong winds and heavy rain to southern China, including Hong Kong , over the weekend.

It prompted the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people in Guangdong province with the region on high alert and hundreds of flights cancelled.

The typhoon – the strongest to make landfall in China so far this year – will dump heavy to torrential rains across much of southern China for two days, authorities said, after ⁠sweeping the province of ⁠Guangdong ​and neighbouring Hong Kong with gale-force winds.

The ⁠year’s 12th tropical cyclone and China’s third this month, Noul, which ​means the glow of sunrise ‌or sunset in Korean, struck ‌the coast of Huidong county about 3.50am, officials ‌said.

It is expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain to nearby provinces such as Jiangxi and Hunan as it moves inland, state media said, with the rains likely to persist until Tuesday.

Extremely heavy to exceptional downpours are expected to lash some areas including the ‌province of Fujian, as the National Meteorological Centre forecast heavy to torrential rain from Sunday until Monday morning across ​much of China’s south.

Authorities urged local governments to pay special attention to flood-prone areas such as zones of mountains and rivers, building sites, valleys and bridges.

Hong Kong’s Observatory said Noul, with maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h (68 mph) near its centre, was moving Sunday into inland Guangdong and weakening progressively.

More than 715,000 people had been relocated for safety in Guangdong province, according to state media. Train services in the province were cancelled for Sunday, according to China News Service.

China’s National Meteorological Center expected parts of southern Guangdong and south-eastern Fujian provinces to experience heavy rain and strong winds. Many trees were seen uprooted in Huilai county, located on the coast of Guangdong province, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Hong Kong’s airport authority said about 350 flights were cancelled Sunday. At least nine people were injured across the city during the typhoon period, according to authorities. Officials said flights will gradually begin resuming on Sunday afternoon.

As Noul approached Hong Kong, parts of a large scaffolding on a high-rise building collapsed on Saturday, police said, although initial reports indicated there were no injuries.

Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration said Noul was bringing rainfall to parts of southern and eastern Taiwan. It was passing over waters south of Taiwan, and was moving away from the island on Saturday.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test
title.zh: “强烈关切”：澳大利亚在中国弹道导弹试验后与中方会晤

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

body.en:
The federal government will spend $4 million on a study to see if it can build a new oil refinery in Western Australia, which could be the nation's first such new facility in six decades.

The study is aimed at buffering the nation to global oil shocks as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to impact supply and fuel costs.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is due to visit Karratha to announce the jointly funded pre-feasibility study for the potential refinery on Tuesday, which his government says could help provide future fuel security.

The project has been proposed by fertiliser producer Perdaman, which currently has a $6.4 billion fertiliser manufacturing facility being built in Karratha.

If the refinery goes ahead, it would be Australia's first since 1960 and would make it the nation's third, along with facilities in Brisbane and Geelong. Those two facilities supply roughly 10 to 20 per cent of the country's fuel.

Australia relies heavily on imported refined fuels. Almost 90 per cent of Australia's daily fuel consumption is imported, much of it brought in as refined product from South Korea, Japan, Singapore, Malaysia and Taiwan.

It used to have more domestic oil refineries, but six of eight facilities closed between 2003 and 2021, after newer, more economical mega-refineries were built across Asia in the 1990s.

Earlier this year, a fire at the Geelong facility, which supplies 10 per cent of the nation's fuel, sparked fears of a fuel supply shortage as Australia was reeling from global oil shocks triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran.

That incident highlighted a structural issue, according to Hussein Dia, a professor of Future Urban Mobility, at Swinburne University of Technology.

"Australia has significantly reduced its refining capacity over recent decades, increasing reliance on long international supply chains. While those systems are generally reliable, events like this show how limited redundancy exists when something goes wrong locally," Dia said at the time.

Experts say Australia needs to accelerate its shift away from liquid fuels , with electrification of transport offering a pathway to greater energy security.

"Improving fuel storage capacity, diversifying energy sources, and expanding electrification of transport would strengthen Australia’s economic resilience to global energy shocks," said University of the Sunshine Coast economics expert Sajid Anwar.

body.en:
Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan faces an open leadership challenge, with Deputy Premier Ben Carroll officially vying for the top role.

"It is clear that the Premier has lost the majority of our Caucus," Carroll said in a statement on Monday as he made his intentions for nomination known.

If she falls, her successor will inherit difficult political circumstances just four months out from Labor's most challenging state election in over a decade.

The party's polling has collapsed as it campaigns for a fourth consecutive term against the rising popularity of One Nation. Polling suggests voters are frustrated with the high cost of living, rising state debt, and infrastructure delays.

Victorian Liberal business spokesperson James Newbury said a change of leadership was unlikely to alter the party's fortunes ahead of the election.

"Changing the leader will not change the problems that Victorians face," Newbury said, urging Labor MPs to hold a vote of no confidence in Allan and trigger an early election.

Carroll has told Allan he will be nominating for leadership of the state Labor Party, despite denying he was seeking the leadership role last month.

"The prospect of a Liberal-One Nation Government that will cut schools, health and front line services is simply too high a risk to ignore," Carroll said.

The challenge will trigger a party-wide ballot. No other candidates have yet emerged.

Victoria's Transport Infrastructure Minister Gabrielle Williams is reportedly being put forward as deputy leader.

Allan said in a letter to Victoria's state secretary, seen by SBS News, that she will stand as a candidate.

MPs reportedly fear that her determination to hang on could plunge the party into chaos, as a leadership ballot requires a vote from the entire Victorian Labor caucus and members which could take weeks.

An opinion poll conducted by Resolve indicated 43 per cent of Victorians prefer Liberal leader Jess Wilson for state premier, compared with 24 per cent who favour Allan.

The primary vote of both major parties was pegged at 27 per cent, with One Nation just behind on 22 per cent.

Zareh Ghazarian, associate professor in politics at Monash University, told SBS News that Allan and Labor's popularity has been falling since former premier Dan Andrews left office. Once a model of stability, the party is now entering "the great unknown".

"This is a very risky position to be in, because we know that when parties go into periods of leadership instability, leadership turmoil, voters turn against them," Ghazarian said.

title.en: Pauline Hanson fails to overturn racial vilification ruling against deputy Greens leader
title.zh: 宝琳·汉森未能推翻针对绿党副领袖的种族诽谤裁决

summary.en: The One Nation leader has lost her appeal two years after the ruling that deemed her comments a "strong form of racism".

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has failed to overturn a court ruling that she made a racist remark when she told a fellow senator to go "back to Pakistan".

After spending much of her decades-long career rejecting accusations of racism, One Nation founder Pauline Hanson has failed to quash a court ruling that she made a racist remark online.

She was found in 2024 to have racially vilified deputy Greens leader Mehreen Faruqi by telling her to "piss off back to Pakistan" in a tweet posted shortly after the death of Queen Elizabeth II.

In his Federal Court decision handed down in 2024, Justice Angus Stewart ruled it was "seriously offensive" and a "strong form of racism".

Senator Hanson launched an appeal against the finding, with her barrister arguing the remarks might not have been pleasant but they did not intimidate people of colour.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The appeal was dismissed by the Full Court of the Federal Court on Monday, nearly four years after the social media post that landed the firebrand politician in hot water.

It came in response to a post on X, formerly Twitter, from Senator Faruqi on the day of the Queen's death in which she offered her condolences to those who knew the monarch.

But she added she could not mourn the passing of the leader of a "racist empire built on stolen lives, land and wealth of colonised peoples".

In a heated retort, Senator Hanson said she was appalled and disgusted by the comments.

"When you immigrated to Australia you took every advantage of this country," she wrote.

The remark was the "ultimate racist slur", Senator Faruqi noted after her victory in the Federal Court two years ago.

The social media stoush isn't the only time the two politicians have clashed, with some of Senator Hanson's more eye-catching stunts in the Senate drawing her colleague's ire.

The Greens senator accused the right-winger of blatant racism and Islamophobia when the latter w ore a burqa into parliament , just six days after the appeal hearing in November.

The 72-year-old has recently come under fire since returning from a European trip, where she was seen holidaying in Italy with billionaire donor Gina Rinehart.

Senator Hanson also met with anti-immigration activist and convicted criminal Tommy Robinson and told a conservative conference Australia had been flooded with migrants.

Since returning, she has attracted criticism for describing domestic violence as a "two-way street" in comments she insists have been taken out of context .

A Roy Morgan poll published on Tuesday showed her anti-immigration party's primary vote had dipped more than 5 percentage points to 22.5 per cent in the space of a week.

body.en:
The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) says taxpayers with straightforward tax affairs can now begin lodging their tax returns, with most income statements and pre-fill information now available.

More than 100 million pieces of data from employers, banks, private health insurers, share registries and government agencies have been loaded into the ATO's systems to help people lodge more accurately and with less effort.

ATO assistant commissioner Anita Challen released a statement saying that most income statements and pre-fill information is now available.

"If you're self-lodging, before you hit submit, take a few extra minutes to check your details to avoid delays and mistakes," she said.

The ATO is also expanding its pre-fill services this year to include income reported through the Taxable Payment Annual Report.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

From late August, contractors in some industries — including construction, cleaning, courier services, information technology, road freight and security — may see that income automatically added to their returns.

Your tax affairs are likely to be straightforward if you're primarily paying tax on salary and wages, with only a small amount of taxable investment income or government payments.

If you're applying for more than basic deductions, or your return includes elements like capital gains, receipt of rental payments and foreign income, your return may not be straightforward.

If you're unsure, you should consult a tax accountant or services such as the ATO's Tax Help or National Tax Clinic for advice.

The ATO is also warning Australians against overclaiming deductions or failing to declare all sources of income.

That includes earnings from side hustles, cash jobs, rental properties and online content creation.

The agency says it uses sophisticated data-matching systems to detect suspicious claims and may delay refunds while returns are investigated.

Taxpayers are also being urged not to simply copy deductions from previous years if their work or circumstances have changed.

The ATO is reminding Australians that the proposed $1,000 standard work-related deduction does not apply this tax time and cannot be claimed until the 2027 tax year.

It is also warning people not to rely on tax advice from artificial intelligence platforms, social media "finfluencers", family or friends without checking official guidance or speaking to a registered tax professional.

Before lodging, the ATO recommends taxpayers check their personal details, bank account and superannuation information are up to date and ensure all pre-filled information is accurate.

title.en: AusAlert emergency warning test: What to do if you didn't receive the alert
title.zh: AusAlert 紧急警报测试：如果您没有收到警报该怎么办

summary.en: People may have had different experiences of the AusAlert test depending on their device, mobile network, settings and location.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
With millions of Australians receiving a loud siren and text message simultaneously across the country for the national AusAlert test, many had prepared their phones ahead of the warning.

AusAlert is a new national emergency warning system being rolled out by the federal government to deliver faster, more reliable alerts during life-threatening events such as bushfires, floods and cyclones.

Australians experienced the system for the first time during a nationwide test on Monday afternoon, and were told to be aware of the 10-second siren.

For many, it sounded at 2pm AEST, 1.30pm ACST and 12pm AWST, with the alert coming out of mobile phones, smartwatches, and tablets.

It's cell-based technology, so compatible devices connected to a tower sounded the alert.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

AusAlert will be officially rolled out in October as a way for emergency agencies to warn people about life-threatening emergencies.

The alert is designed to ensure warnings are not missed, so it will override "do not disturb" or silent mode settings.

People who didn't want to receive the notification were advised in advance to turn off the device or put it in aeroplane mode.

Authorities also advised people who rely on concealed mobile phones for their safety to switch them off before Monday's test.

If your device was switched on and not in aeroplane mode and it still didn't come through, there may be a few reasons why.

It could be because it wasn't connected to a tower in those 10 seconds, it's not a compatible device or an older phone, or hasn't had system updates.

Authorities have a fairly simple reply: don't panic, it's just a test — but any glitches could give them some tips on how to manage an actual national emergency.
